selected_mechanism.name: TCEQ data-center permit pause
selected_mechanism.definition: A hold on data-center environmental permit issuance that links TCEQ decisions to completion of ERCOT review and audit evidence.
selected_mechanism.texas_scope: TCEQ data-center permitting in Texas. The directive is broader than the specific ERCOT RFI respondent classes; ERCOT is not all Texas.

news_trigger.verbatim_span: to pause the issuance of all permits related to data center projects until ERCOT completes its review.

source.title: September 21 letter to TCEQ Executive Director Kelly Keel
claims_supported: Direction to pause data-center permit issuance until ERCOT completes review.
TCEQ must align permitting decisions with the directive and use audit information.
TCEQ compliance update to Governor due October 19, 2026.
The letter does not specify a reopening date or promise approval after review.

layers.name: Impact review

layers.function: Collects project information through utility submission of developer responses in RIOO.

primary_source.title: M-B091426-01 State and Community Impact RFI
claims_supported: ERCOT collects information about power, water, ownership, incentives and community effects.
Utility submits developer response through RIOO with a notarized attestation by 5 p.m. Central Prevailing Time October 12, 2026.

ERCOT may request follow-up information and expects an impact report by December 10, 2026.
The RFI covers specified not-yet-energized Batch Zero projects and substantiated medium loads; it is separate from the September 9 eligibility RFI.

chokepoint.binary_decision: Issue a permit or withhold it; the directive requires withholding issuance until ERCOT completes review. This is not a claim of unrestricted agency discretion or automatic approval after review.
chokepoint.post_decision_phrase: issue a permit or withhold it
chokepoint.why_asymmetric: Developers and audit respondents can supply information but cannot substitute for the permitting agency issuing a permit.

selected_mechanism.texas_consequence: Texas AI data-center campuses needing TCEQ permits face an environmental approval dependency tied to the grid review. Not every data center is assumed to run AI.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The issuing office seeks a fuller power, water and community-impact record. Editorial inference: linking permit issuance to another review creates timing dependence without a fixed reopening date in the directive. This evaluates process legibility rather than a preferred policy outcome.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Inspect the October 19 compliance update for implementation of the hold and use of audit evidence. Do not treat it or the separate RFI/report dates as automatic reopening.

next_check.what: TCEQ compliance update on the September 21 directive
next_check.date_or_window: 2026-10-19; delivery to Governor required, public release date not established

public_policy_context.competing_effects: More information before decisions is the stated benefit; dependence on an unfinished review with no calendar reopening promise is the procedural tradeoff. Neither is a project-specific impact finding.

evidence_gaps: No TCEQ implementation bulletin or delivered October 19 update was established in this run. The post describes the signed directive, not completed agency implementation.
No universal release test, public-release schedule for the TCEQ update, reopening date, or guaranteed permit approval is established.
The RFI scope must not be substituted for the broader directive scope.
The directive is not a court ruling on executive authority, and this analysis makes no legal enforceability finding.
selected_mechanism.prior_coverage_comparison: September 11 covered Batch Zero eligibility; September 18 covered PGRR144 as-built models. This September 21 trigger adds a new TCEQ environmental permit layer and a different controlling decision.

required_post_phrases: issue a permit or withhold it

verified_facts.claim: September 21, 2026 directive pauses TCEQ issuance until ERCOT completes its review; post uses September 21st.
Governor seeks information on grid reliability, water and community effects before agency decisions.
TCEQ letter addresses Executive Director Kelly Keel and requires October 19, 2026 compliance update; post uses October 19th.
No fixed permit reopening date or automatic approval after review appears in the letter. Editorial inference: a developer response alone does not complete ERCOT review.
Utility submission through RIOO and TWDB water-response routing operate as described in the layers.
Covered RFI responses due October 12, 2026 and impact report expected no later than December 10, 2026; post uses October 12th and December 10th.

RFI covers specified Batch Zero data-center projects and substantiated proposed loads at least 25 MW and less than 75 MW, with energization conditions; directive addresses all data-center permits sought from TCEQ.
Conditional Texas AI relevance: an AI campus that needs a covered data-center permit faces the same permit dependency. No claim that all data centers run AI.
Procedural inference: a hold pending another review couples approval timing to that review; stated information benefit is distinct from proof of a specific campus impact.

gate_notes.news_tie: Signed September 21 letter refetched on September 25, four days old.
gate_notes.anatomizable_depth: Four connected functions with named institutional controllers.
gate_notes.primary_source_each_layer: Signed letter and ERCOT issued notice re-fetched successfully; full sources retained locally with hashes.
gate_notes.texas_consequence: Environmental permit issuance for Texas AI campuses requiring covered permits.
gate_notes.chokepoint_asymmetry: TCEQ controls issuing versus withholding permits; audit respondents cannot issue permits.
gate_notes.mechanism_not_actor: The selected object is the conditional permit hold, not an officeholder profile.
gate_notes.not_recent_repeat: September 11 covered Batch Zero eligibility; September 18 covered PGRR144 as-built models. This September 21 trigger adds a new TCEQ environmental permit layer and a different controlling decision.
gate_notes.political_neutrality: No electoral motives, candidate comparisons, party preferences or preferred policy outcomes. Score concerns evidence and writing only.

discovery_context: Four lanes searched in September 11-25 window. Grid review, water-reporting follow-up, state environmental permitting and procurement calendars guided discovery only. No broadening required.
selection_reason: Signed primary directive, operational primary data-flow notice, independent trigger corroboration, named permit controller and near-term compliance check make this the strongest evidence package.
